# なる family — ways of expressing change

**[なる](<../grammar/naru.md> "Become.")**
:   The bare verb 'become' — the head of this family. In real sentences it takes a frame: noun or na-adjective + になる, i-adjective + くなる, verb + ようになる.

**[になる](<../grammar/ni-naru.md> "Become X; intransitive change into a noun or na-adjective state")**
:   Change into a noun or na-adjective state: 医者になる・元気になる。What comes before decides the frame — に after nouns and na-adjectives; くなる after i-adjectives.

**[くなる](<../grammar/ku-naru.md> "Become a stated i-adjective quality; marks a change of state")**
:   Change in an i-adjective quality — drop the い, add くなる: 寒くなる・高くなった (いい→よくなる)。The i-adjective partner of になる.

**[ようになる](<../grammar/you-ni-naru.md> "Come to do something or reach a new ability or habitual state")**
:   A change that arrives over time with verbs — new ability, habit, or state: 日本語が話せるようになった。For 'came to' or 'can now', not a simple change of state.

**[ことになる](<../grammar/koto-ni-naru.md> "Come to be decided or arranged; outcome is not solely speaker-controlled")**
:   An outcome decided by others or by circumstances: 大阪に転勤することになった。An arrangement, not a gradual change — and not only your own choice.
